ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Morphine, $C_{17}H_{19}NO_3$, has a $K_b = 8.0 \times 10^{-7}$. If a 0.00100 M solution of morphine is prepared, what pH range is expected?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows the structural formula of morphine, containing a nitrogen-containing methyl-substituted amine site and multiple oxygen-containing functional groups; this problem's calculation mainly uses the Kb and concentration given in the question stem. Treat morphine as a weak base B: B + H2O ⇌ BH+ + OH−. Initial concentration [B] = 0.00100 M, [OH−] = 0; at equilibrium [OH−] = [BH+] = x, [B] = 0.00100 − x. Therefore Kb = x^2/(0.00100 − x) = 8.0 × 10^-7. Since Kb is relatively small, approximate x ≈ sqrt(KbC) = sqrt((8.0 × 10^-7)(1.00 × 10^-3)) = sqrt(8.0 × 10^-10) ≈ 2.8 × 10^-5 M. So pOH = −log(2.8 × 10^-5) ≈ 4.55, pH = 14.00 − 4.55 ≈ 9.45. 9.45 falls within the range from 8 to 10.
